What exists and what is missing

The source is PrincetonUniversity/athena, pinned commit
 e47fabb7dd5efb22e1e2c7ff193148d723e3e952.
Existing solver/athena_wind provides a serial, single-MeshBlock spherical-polar
hydro generator, frozen observation parser/units, gravity, inner hydrodynamic
inflow, native and compatible output, and finite CPU/wall/memory caps. Its coarse,
medium and fine hydro runs completed. Independent HLLC fluxes, spherical geometry
and RK integration are established. A separate pinned Athena Brio-Wu MHD build
also exists; that confirms MHD availability, not this solar boundary treatment.

The generator explicitly rejects MAGNETIC_FIELDS_ENABLED. Its inner callback
ignores FaceField. Initial total energy omits magnetic energy; capture, probes and
snapshots have no magnetic state and output B=0. x3i_boundary.hpp reads four
fields only, with no inductive EMFs, new speed/thermodynamic closure, or CME cone
semantics. Reusing it without explicit parity checks would silently ignore newer
physical configuration flags. The current strict-floors patch edits only
adiabatic_hydro.cpp: MHD has its own density/pressure/energy floors in
adiabatic_mhd.cpp, requiring separate counted diagnostics or pre-floor hard errors.
The existing build uses HLLC and no -b; a separate MHD derivative needs -b and an
MHD flux such as HLLD, preserving the hydro build and inputs.

Pinned Athena Field owns staggered FaceField b and edge-centered EdgeField e.
Field::CT updates every active face, including inner and outer normal radial
faces, by exact geometric edge circulations with dB/dt=-curl(E). Its integrated
face-area divergence is preserved algebraically if initially zero and if active
faces are changed only by that shared-edge update. Public enrollment functions
include user ghost-boundary callbacks but no user edge-EMF callback. The normal
face in a physical boundary is active CT data; a ghost callback must not overwrite
b.x1f(...,is), b.x1f(...,ie+1), or analogous active latitude faces.

Minimum correct magnetic initialization

For a bounded first control, a particularly simple exactly solenoidal initial
field is possible without a 3D projection: area-average the corrected frozen
initial Br over each angular pixel and define its radial flux
  Phi_r(i,j,k)=r0^2 * <Br(r0)>_(j,k) * DeltaOmega_(j,k)
identically at every radial face i. Set angular-face fluxes to zero. Then each
cell's radial outward/inward fluxes cancel exactly and tangential flux is zero;
B_r=Phi_r/Face1Area is divergence-free on Athena's actual face geometry even for
nonaxisymmetric mixed-polarity maps. On the full sphere retain the recorded
monopole removal. In a wedge, flux through the inner and outer shell boundaries
balances; the wedge need not have zero radial flux separately.

This initializer is unretarded and initially untwisted. It deliberately differs
from the production retarded Parker guess. Adding a point-sampled Parker Bphi to
angularly varying Br/v generally creates nonzero divergence through its longitude
derivative. Retarding different map epochs at different radii also makes radial
flux vary with radius. Neither is a valid CT initializer merely because its
point formula resembles a Parker spiral.

If matching a twisted initial state is important, construct edge-integrated vector
potential and set ALL face fluxes by its discrete curl, using Athena's exact
edge/area metrics (the upstream field_loop_poles generator demonstrates this).
A discrete constrained projection with prescribed inner normal flux is an
alternative, but brings a further global solve and boundary choices. Either
method changes the pointwise guessed field and that change must be recorded.
After face initialization call CalculateCellCenteredField and initialize total
energy including 0.5|Bcc|^2 in Athena units. Initialize/synchronize all integration
registers consistently and measure the native face-flux divergence before step1.

The untwisted initializer is cheap but needs an initialization sensitivity/spinup
check before scientific PN comparison. Bulk advection transit time alone cannot
prove loss of initial magnetic information: MHD characteristic speeds and latitude
boundary communication matter. Starting earlier with a clamped first WSA map is a
possible numerical spinup assumption, not additional observed forcing.

Correct evolving inner Br and electric-field closure

Choose a documented angular area-remap of the frozen Br maps onto the ACTUAL
Athena radial boundary faces, preserving phase, solar frame and rotation. Denote
this target flux Phi_target(t). Preserve measured-derived v/n/T forcing and its
selected closure separately. Do not interpolate the centered EMF CSV into ghosts
and call that exact CT map driving: it leaves the previously measured29.1%/31.3%
source qdot residual in latitude bands±30/±60deg. CT would still preserve its
initial discrete divergence, but its evolved normal field would not reproduce
the prescribed WSA sequence. Forcing target Br directly afterward would inject
divergence into the adjacent active cells.

The required inner edge data are circulations
  Ltheta*Etheta on theta-directed edges at r0, longitude faces;
  Lphi*Ephi on phi-directed edges at r0, latitude faces.
Their oriented curl must satisfy on each boundary pixel
  dPhi_target/dt = -(Lphi_north*Ephi_north-Lphi_south*Ephi_south)
                  +(Ltheta_east*Etheta_east-Ltheta_west*Etheta_west)
when expressed in Athena's increasing-colatitude indexing (use ct.cpp as the
sign/index authority). This is the exact integrated Faraday equation; reversing
latitude indexing requires reversing the associated differences, not Etheta's
physical direction. Apply one value to each shared periodic edge, including the
inner/latitude-boundary corner edges. Active normal Br then evolves only by CT.

Most robust: recompute the surface minimum-norm curl closure with the target
Athena face areas and edge lengths, including the FULL inertial derivative
  partial_t Br_inertial = partial_t Br_Carr - Omega*partial_phi Br_Carr.
One can retain a physically selected Parker/rotation EMF and solve only for the
remaining discrete-curl residual. Remove and record the full-sphere l=0 component
of the target flux derivative; a globally smooth surface curl cannot change total
signed flux. Use a full-sphere auxiliary surface grid with the same angular
spacing as the wedge, then restrict its edges, rather than imposing arbitrary
zero edge EMF at wedge latitude limits. A target-grid FFT-longitude/tridiagonal-
latitude solve remains small compared with a 3D timestep. No new large library is
required. Preserve the gauge/nonuniqueness caveat: Br changes determine the
surface curl, not an observed or unique electric field.

Even native staggered source E is not identically Athena's exact geometry.
The old closure's longitude factor is1/[r*cos(beta)*dphi], whereas exact edge/area
curl uses dbeta/[r*(sin(beta_hi)-sin(beta_lo))*dphi]. Their ratio is
 dbeta/[2*sin(dbeta/2)]=1.00005077137 at2deg, or1.00286150751 at15deg.
Applying Athena's exact metric to actual native correction faces, source days
22..32, gives residual/qdot RMS3.3674e-5 in±30 and3.2957e-5 in±60, compared with
1.3e-13 for the original source operator. This tiny difference is distinct from
the approximately30% center-reconstruction error and supports recomputing the
closure with the actual consumer operator. Rotating remaps and time integration
introduce additional independent differences.

Time and code hooks

The current Athena wind input selects rk2, verified to be Heun/SSPRK(2,2).
Boundary primitives are evaluated at stage end times by PhysicalBoundary; EMFs
are constructed in CalculateEMF via ComputeCornerE before communication and CT.
A separate optional hook immediately after that construction can replace ONLY
the physical inner tangential edge EMFs. It must receive the actual stage time,
full dt and stage weights, and occur before edge communication/CT. Single-block,
no-AMR, no-orbital-advection scope makes this manageable. UserWorkInLoop runs
only after the full timestep and is too late to prescribe an RK-stage EMF.
An alternative hook immediately before CT needs equally explicit stage data and
shared-edge handling; simply writing e in a ghost callback is overwritten later.

At minimum, sample interval-constant Carrington correction using the left map
interval at the actual RK RHS time, with the correct right derivative at a map
knot, and limit steps to map knots. Scalar/Br maps remain linearly interpolated
in Carrington time. Inertial rotation still evolves a clamped Carrington map;
only the daily-change correction becomes zero outside the measured interval,
not the total Parker/rotation EMF.

A stronger exact-tracking construction computes the target face-flux increment
Phi_target(t+dt)-Phi_target(t) and fits the RK-weighted mean edge circulation to
that increment using the exact discrete curl. For SSPRK2, using an interval-
average imposed boundary EMF in both stages can reproduce that increment without
resetting normal faces; or correct the RK-weighted mean of a chosen time-varying
Parker EMF. The latter preserves its chosen curl-free component. This requires
explicit time-integration tests, especially rotating interpolation knots; it is
a design option, not an implemented or validated hook.

Ghost magnetic values and conservation

Inner primitives can use the chosen v/n/T and tangential B consistent with E:
  Bphi=Etheta/vr, Btheta=-Ephi/vr for purely radial velocity,
where total Etheta already includes the Parker term. Athena E code units are
E[nT AU/day]*1e-9/BUNIT, with velocity in AU/day and BUNIT in Tesla.
If transverse v is used, derive the full ideal-MHD E=-v cross B relation.
Construct radial ghost faces recursively from discrete zero-divergence, anchored
to the CT-evolved active normal face; never reset that anchor to a map sample.
Outer/latitude ghost fills must likewise leave active normal faces untouched.

Overriding edge EMF after a Riemann solve does not automatically make its radial
energy flux the corresponding Poynting flux. The imposed S_r is
 (Etheta*Bphi-Ephi*Btheta)/mu0 in SI. Use consistent boundary face states and
record the discrepancy between the imposed CT electric work and the conservative
MHD boundary energy flux; if it exceeds the accepted truncation tolerance,
apply a separately reviewed, documented boundary Poynting-flux correction before
hydro integration. Also audit mass and Maxwell stress fluxes. This is an
externally driven boundary, not evidence that an arbitrary magnetic-energy
change is an unrecorded numerical source. Recheck radial fast Mach with the
actual tangential correction and selected density/B/T scalings before assuming
all characteristics are prescribed inflow.

Bounded decision gates if the fallback becomes necessary

First validate stationary and smoothly rotating manufactured face-flux maps on a
small angular grid, with native face divergence near roundoff, target-Br tracking,
periodic-seam consistency, RK stage times and complete energy/work ledgers.
Then a single-MeshBlock48x8x48 short wind pilot under the existing serial caps is
a reasonable finite test, followed by matched-grid comparison only if it passes.
A constant/radial magnetized geometry benchmark should precede actual WSA data.
CT controls the face divergence; it does not establish thermodynamic positivity,
flux convergence, a trustworthy CME forecast, or latitude-domain independence.
Hydro runtime is not a measured MHD runtime, and no resource forecast is claimed.
The current independent hydro sequence itself has a10.47% medium-to-fine PN mean
flux shift. A future low-divergence CT solution must still pass physical forcing
